title: ASBC & CIBD 2026 Global Brewing and Distilling Congress
organiser: American Society of Brewing Chemists and Chartered Institute of Brewers and Distillers
summary: First joint congress of ASBC and CIBD, themed Global Brewing and Distilling Innovation: Shaping the Future Together, spanning beer, distilled spirits and wine. The two bodies bring roughly 4000 technical members across 90 and 40 countries respectively, which makes this the densest technical gathering of the year for fermentation science.

title: Brews & Spirits Expo 2026
location: KTPO Convention Centre, Whitefield, Bengaluru, India
summary: Seventh edition of India's alcobev trade show: brand owners, brewers, winemakers, distillers, equipment makers and technology providers, with a conference and awards programme alongside the floor. The single densest gathering of Indian beverage decision makers in the calendar.

title: BrauBeviale 2026
summary: Europe's working trade fair for beverage production: raw materials, technology, logistics and marketing. Historically one of the highest-yield surfaces for finding brewing technology vendors, since the exhibitor list is published in full.

title: Master Brewers Conference 2026
organiser: Master Brewers Association of the Americas
location: Virginia Beach Convention Center, Virginia, United States
summary: The technical brewing conference: sessions, workshops and an exhibit hall aimed at production brewers rather than marketers. Exact dates are not stated on the conference page, so none are recorded here; registration runs to 24 October 2026.

title: Unified Wine & Grape Symposium
organiser: ASEV and California Association of Winegrape Growers
summary: The largest wine industry trade show and technical conference in the Americas, held each January, covering viticulture, winemaking and increasingly the data and sensing side of both.

title: Anuga FoodTec
summary: Food and beverage process technology fair covering automation, filling, packaging and digitalisation. Relevant because the brewery automation vendors exhibit here under a food-and-beverage banner rather than a brewing one.

title: IBD events and courses
summary: Rolling programme of technical events, courses and webinars for brewing and distilling. Mixed in-person and online, which makes it one of the few reliably reachable technical programmes from outside the UK.

title: drinktec
summary: The world's largest beverage and liquid food technology fair, held every few years; the 2025 edition drew participants from 164 countries. Sources disagree on whether the next edition is 2028 or 2029, so no dates are recorded here until the organiser confirms.

title: Vine to Mind Symposium 2026
organiser: Harvard Data Science Initiative and UC Davis
location: UC Davis and Napa Valley, California, United States
summary: The clearest wine-meets-data-science programme running, held on the 50th anniversary of the Judgment of Paris. Named AI sessions include Tomorrow's Grapevines: AI-Powered Genomics and Breeding, Current State and Moonshots: AI from Vineyard to End Consumer, Data Science Tools for the Future of Wine, and a conversation on AI and Wine: Excitements and Cautionary Tales.

title: Craft Brewers Conference & BrewExpo America 2026
location: Pennsylvania Convention Center, Philadelphia, United States
summary: The US craft brewing industry's main annual gathering, shortened to three days for the 2026 edition. Already past for this year; listed so the cycle is visible when planning the next one.

title: How AI Is Transforming Breweries: Craft Beer School
summary: Ankur Napa session for Craft Beer School on where AI actually lands in a working brewery, and where it does not. Recorded and freely watchable.

title: The Modern Brewer Podcast, Ep 24: AI in Brewing
summary: Ankur Napa on what AI is for a brewer, which tools and systems it can realistically replace, real deployments, and the blunt question of whether it replaces brewers.

title: Bridging the Gap Between Artificial Intelligence and Brewing
summary: Ankur Napa talk for Brewer World making the case that brewing domain knowledge is what makes brewing data useful, delivered from the position of having done both jobs.
